title: TEDEdb: A multicohort analysis and resource for transposable element differential expression in cancer.
publicationName: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
journalName: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
snippet: The human genome consists of nearly 50% repetitive DNA, referred to for decades as "junk DNA." These repetitive sequences, usually under the strict control of epigenetic silencing, can become aberrantly expressed in cancer.
